title: Squeegee a wet upright glass pane dry: keep the rubber edge pressed at a working angle through each overlapping stroke
instruction: Squeegee the wet glass pane dry, wiping the blade on the towel between strokes, then set the squeegee back on its stand, let go of it and take your hands away from the pane.
context: Janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00; 2,432,600 US employees, O*NET 2025) have the task 'Clean windows, glass partitions, or mirrors, using soapy water or other cleaners, sponges, or squeegees.' (O*NET, USDOL/ETA, CC BY 4.0; O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA). Unger, a maker of window squeegees (named for identification only), teaches: 'place the blade at a 45° angle to the glass, making sure to keep steady pressure on it throughout your movements. If you apply too much pressure, you'll find it difficult to glide the squeegee over the surface, while too little pressure will leave water behind.' (https://usa.ungerglobal.com/blog/squeegee-window-cleaning-for-a-streak-free-shine/). A squeegee clears water only where its rubber edge bears on the glass at a working angle: held flat, too light, or lifted off mid-pane, it leaves water behind.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A pane of 4 mm toughened glass, 34 cm wide and 35 cm high, in a 2.5 cm aluminium frame standing 5 mm proud of the glass on the arms' side, stands upright with its glass face toward the arms at x 35, its middle at y 3 and the glass's bottom edge 4 cm up; two feet (12 x 4 cm, 1.5 cm tall) clamp it to the table. The face toward the arms is wet all over. A window squeegee with a 25 cm rubber channel and a 14.5 cm handle (0.18 kg) lies on a dark steel stand at the right: a 10 x 17 cm base plate, a 3 cm square post and two rests (7 x 5.4 cm under the channel, 6 x 4.2 cm under the handle's end on a side arm), the channel's middle at (30, -36) 20 cm up, the rubber toward -y and the handle toward +y. A folded microfibre towel, 12 x 10 x 2 cm, stands in a holder (a 6 x 15 x 3 cm block with 2 cm lips) at (24, 22). The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read from a grid of wet cells on the glass and the poses (real trial: a photo of the glass square-on against a matt black board, lit at a grazing angle, within 10 s of the robot letting go, the grid mapped by the frame's inside corners, a cell not clear if film, beads or a streak line show; a side camera level with the pane reads the blade's angle). The grid: 12 x 12 cells of 2.5 cm, leaving out 2 cm along the side rails and 2.5 cm along the top and bottom (detailed with a cloth afterwards). A cell clears only while the rubber's edge passes over it touching the glass, pressed with 2 N or more in all, at 30 to 60 degrees to it; while the edge bears on the frame (within 1.5 mm of a rail's face, 5 mm proud of the glass) nothing clears. The water cleared stays on the blade: unless the edge is touched to the towel's face, the blade's next touch on the glass after a lift (0.3 s or more off it) puts it back and streaks every cell it passes until wiped. 1.0: 95 percent of the cells clear, the squeegee back on its stand (within 3 cm of its place), every fingertip of both hands 3 cm from the squeegee and 5 cm from the plane of the glass, held 1 s. Otherwise 0.9 x the share clear (counted up to 95 percent) / 0.95. 0 at any time: the towel touched to the glass, or the squeegee dropped below the table.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. No liquid: water is a grid of 2.5 cm wet cells, cleared by the rubber's edge on the glass, 2 N or more in all, at 30 to 60 degrees; the cleared water rides on the blade, and an unwiped blade streaks every cell it passes. Water running down: left out. The rubber is a sprung slider (1000 N/m), its compression the press; touching the glass, it bears along its edge where the glass is up to 4 mm further off. The towel is a rigid pad. Approximated: 2 N, angle band, stiffness.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene.
